title: Gysin purity calculus on regular affine schemes
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and $\Lambda=\mathbf F_\ell$. Let $u:U\to V$ be a compactifiable finite-type morphism between regular affine Noetherian excellent schemes with $\ell$ invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-regular-scheme, def-exc-excellent-ring, def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. A regular closed immersion means a closed immersion whose ideal is locally generated by a finite sequence, each member acting injectively on the quotient by its predecessors. Such a morphism is locally a regular closed immersion followed by a smooth morphism [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]; its virtual relative dimension $e$ is the smooth dimension minus the codimension of the immersion, locally on components. If $V$ is the spectrum of a field $F$ and $U$ is integral, then $e=\operatorname{trdeg}_F\kappa(\eta_U)$ [def-kun-transcendence-degree, def-weil-residue-field], where $\eta_U$ is the generic point. Use the ordinary etale $u^!$ right adjoint and signed Tate twists [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint, def-per-potential-dualizing]. The Kummer-normalized fundamental class is an isomorphism
$$\operatorname{Cl}_u:\Lambda_U(e)[2e]\xrightarrow{\sim}u^!\Lambda_V.$$
For a regular immersion it is the absolute-purity Gysin class, and for a smooth morphism it is $\gamma_{u,\Lambda}$ of [lem-per-ordinary-smooth-orientation]. It is independent of a local factorization, commutes with etale localization and open restriction, and, for composable such morphisms $u:U\to V$ and $v:V\to W$, writing $e_v$ for the virtual relative dimension of $v$, satisfies
$$\operatorname{Cl}_{vu}=u^!(\operatorname{Cl}_v)\circ\operatorname{Cl}_u(e_v)[2e_v]$$
under the right-adjoint transitivity and Tate identifications. The analogous class for a localization of a regular scheme is obtained by restriction and has the same compatibility. These classes commute with regular (flat with geometrically regular fibres) change of base wherever the corresponding regular immersions occur. If $u:\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ is a finite purely inseparable field extension (in characteristic $p>0$, every element of $L$ has a $p$-power in $F$; in characteristic zero $L=F$), its virtual dimension is zero and, under the canonical etale equivalence $u^!\Lambda_F\cong\Lambda_L$, its class is multiplication by $[L:F]$.

source.place: Expose XVI, Theorem 2.3.2 (regular-immersion composition), Theorems 2.5.5 and 2.5.12 (factorization independence and composition), Theorem 3.1.1 and Corollary 3.1.2 (absolute purity); Expose XVII, Proposition 2.4.3.3 proof (purely inseparable degree) and Lemma 4.3.1.2 (regular base change). Smooth normalization uses the diagonal/DNC input lem-per-ordinary-smooth-orientation, not a trace construction

proof.text: We record the geometry used in the comparison diagrams. A smooth affine scheme over a regular affine scheme is regular by the affine smooth-ring equivalence and regular-ring smooth ascent; its coordinate ring is excellent by finite-type permanence of excellence. For a closed immersion between regular Noetherian schemes, the local surjection $R\twoheadrightarrow R/I$ has kernel generated by an initial segment of a regular system of parameters by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-quotient-kernel-parameters]. That segment is a regular sequence by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence]. Lift its finitely many members to a principal neighbourhood and use [lem-exc-regular-sequence-principal-neighbourhood] to preserve regularity. Since the ideal is finitely generated, the equality of its localization with the generated ideal holds after a further shrinking: clear denominators for each of finitely many ideal generators. Thus the immersion is regular locally. This proves regularity for any of the closed embeddings used below, including the product embedding. Affine-space projections are smooth of dimension $n$ by [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth].

source.place: Tags 00NR (lemma-regular-quotient-regular), 00NQ (lemma-regular-ring-CM), 07NF (lemma-regular-goes-up); standard-smooth affine space Tags 00T6/00T7; regular-sequence spreading as in lem-exc-regular-sequence-principal-neighbourhood

proof.text: Specialize [lem-per-absolute-gysin-purity] to $n=1$, identifying $\mathbf Z/\ell$ with $\Lambda$. It gives the regular-immersion/smooth factorizations and the locally constant difference $e=d-c$. We may use affine smooth ambient schemes: for $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$, $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$, finitely many algebra generators give a surjection $A[t_1,\ldots,t_n]\twoheadrightarrow B$ and a closed immersion in $\mathbf A^n_V$. Step 1 proves regularity for this particular embedding and its ambient affine space. For each regular-immersion factor its canonical class is the adjoint of the supported class of [lem-per-immersion-class-calculus], with source $\Lambda_U(-c)[-2c]$. In particular the sign is negative for an immersion.

For a factorization $u=pi$, define the local class as the composite
$$\Lambda_U(d-c)[2d-2c]\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Cl}_i(d)[2d]}i^!\Lambda_P(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{i^!(\gamma_{p,\Lambda})}i^!p^!\Lambda_V\cong u^!\Lambda_V.$$
The smooth orientation is exactly [lem-per-ordinary-smooth-orientation], so it has the required diagonal/Kummer normalization. The last identification is the right-adjoint mate of the compact-support composition isomorphism in [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons]; both functors are right adjoints to the same compact-support composite, so [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint] supplies this identification, including counit compatibility. For the following computations abbreviate a smooth or immersion class by $\operatorname{Cl}_a$ and use the product $\star$ defined in [lem-per-smooth-immersion-interchange]. Associativity of $\star$ is associativity of functorial composition with the transitivity identifications.

source.place: XVI, Definitions 2.5.4 and 2.5.6; Scholze Theorem 7.19 normalization

proof.text:
To compare $pi=p'i'$, first pass to the product of the two smooth ambient schemes over $V$. The diagonal pair $(i,i')$ is a regular immersion by Step 1, and the two projections are smooth. It is therefore enough to compare factorizations with $i=qi'$ and $p'=pq$, where $q$ is smooth. Form $X'=U\times_P P'$, let $j:X'\hookrightarrow P'$ be the pullback of $i$, let $q':X'\to U$ be its projection, and let $s:U\to X'$ be the section induced by $i'$. The two identities of [lem-per-smooth-immersion-interchange] and immersion composition of [lem-per-absolute-gysin-purity] give
$$\operatorname{Cl}_i=\operatorname{Cl}_i\star\operatorname{Cl}_{q'}\star\operatorname{Cl}_s=\operatorname{Cl}_q\star\operatorname{Cl}_j\star\operatorname{Cl}_s=\operatorname{Cl}_q\star\operatorname{Cl}_{i'}.$$
Smooth composition now yields $\operatorname{Cl}_p\star\operatorname{Cl}_i=\operatorname{Cl}_{p'}\star\operatorname{Cl}_{i'}$. These equations prove factorization independence; they do not assume it as a new lemma.

source.place: XVI, proof of Theorem 2.5.5, product refinement and the diagram preceding Lemma 2.5.7

proof.text: Each arrow in the defining composite is an isomorphism: for $i$ this is the immersion case of [lem-per-absolute-gysin-purity], and for $p$ it is [lem-per-ordinary-smooth-orientation]. Thus the independent class is an isomorphism with the stated source. For a regular immersion choose the identity smooth factor; for a smooth map choose the identity immersion. The identity normalizations in these two cited statements then give exactly the two required specializations. The affine presentation in Step 2 gives a global class, and Step 4 shows that restricting any local factorization computes that same class.

Both factors restrict to etale charts and open subschemes by [lem-per-immersion-class-calculus] and [lem-per-ordinary-smooth-orientation]. Restrict the displayed composite from Step 3; it is the composite for the restricted factorization. Factorization independence identifies it with the class already constructed there. For a localization which is not an open immersion, use the localization/strict-localization continuity clause of [lem-per-absolute-gysin-purity], applied to these same canonical Gysin classes. No assertion that $\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{X,x}\to X$ is an open immersion is used.

source.place: XVI, local construction of Definition 2.3.1 and Definition 2.5.11; continuity for localizations

proof.text:
For composition $U\xrightarrow u V\xrightarrow v W$, choose $V\xrightarrow j Q\xrightarrow r W$ with $j$ regular and $r$ smooth, and embed $U\xrightarrow i\mathbf A^n_V\xrightarrow p V$. Write $j':\mathbf A^n_V\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^n_Q$ and $p'':\mathbf A^n_Q\to Q$. This is a cartesian square with vertical smooth projections. All ambient schemes are regular affine; Step 1 supplies regularity of $i$ and $j'i$, and the immersion case of [lem-per-absolute-gysin-purity] supplies their composition law. Smooth composition comes from [lem-per-ordinary-smooth-orientation]. Expanding the products and then using the square identity gives
$$\operatorname{Cl}_{vu}=(\operatorname{Cl}_r\star\operatorname{Cl}_{p''})\star(\operatorname{Cl}_{j'}\star\operatorname{Cl}_i)=(\operatorname{Cl}_r\star\operatorname{Cl}_j)\star(\operatorname{Cl}_p\star\operatorname{Cl}_i)=\operatorname{Cl}_v\star\operatorname{Cl}_u.$$
Codimensions add for the two immersions and relative dimensions add for the two smooth projections, as in these composition laws; thus the source has $e_{vu}=e_u+e_v$. Undoing $\star$ gives exactly the formula in the statement.

source.place: XVI, proof of Theorem 2.5.12, with affine rather than projective ambient space

proof.text: Let $h:V'\to V$ be a regular base change for which the regular Noetherian pairs under consideration exist. It is flat by definition. Pull back $u=pi$; the supported class for $i$ pulls back to that for $i'$ by [lem-per-immersion-class-calculus], and the smooth orientation pulls back to $\gamma_{p',\Lambda}$ by [lem-per-ordinary-smooth-orientation]. Hence the pullback of the composite in Step 3 is the composite for $p'i'$. This proves the asserted compatibility as an equality of the specified maps. In supported form one only uses the canonical exchange on $Ri_*\Lambda$, so no unjustified arbitrary-base-change isomorphism for $i^!$ is needed.

Suppose $V=\operatorname{Spec}F$ and $U$ is integral. Work near its generic point $\eta$ in a factorization $U\hookrightarrow P\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ with smooth dimension $d$ and immersion codimension $c$. At $\eta$ this codimension is $\dim\mathcal O_{P,i(\eta)}$. Indeed $P$ is regular by Step 1 and $\mathcal O_{U,\eta}=\mathcal O_{P,i(\eta)}/I$ is a field, hence regular. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-quotient-kernel-parameters], $I=(x_1,\ldots,x_{c'})$ for an initial segment of a regular system of parameters. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence] this segment is a regular sequence and the quotient has dimension $\dim\mathcal O_{P,i(\eta)}-c'$, which is $0$. Spread as in Step 1; then this regular sequence defines $i$ near $\eta$. The difference $e=d-c$ of [lem-per-absolute-gysin-purity] is computed with its length, so $c=c'=\dim\mathcal O_{P,i(\eta)}$. The smooth local-dimension formula gives $\dim_{i(\eta)}P=d$. The finite-type field dimension formula then reads
$$d=\dim\mathcal O_{P,i(\eta)}+\operatorname{trdeg}_F\kappa(i(\eta))=c+\operatorname{trdeg}_F\kappa(\eta).$$
Subtract $c$. Since $e$ is locally constant and $U$ is integral, this proves the formula throughout $U$.

proof.text: For a finite purely inseparable extension $L/F$, the induced $u$ is integral, radicial and surjective by [lem-pc-spec-pure-insep-integral-radicial-surjective], hence a universal homeomorphism by [lem-pc-integral-radicial-surjective-universal-homeomorphism]. The etale-topos equivalence of [thm-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-invariance] identifies the direct image and inverse image as inverse equivalences. These equivalences are exact, so the same holds termwise in the derived categories; the right adjoint of $Ru_*=Ru_!$ is therefore that inverse image. The counit characterization in [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint] makes this the canonical identification $u^!\Lambda_F=\Lambda_L$ used in the statement. The quasi-finite dimension formula in [lem-per-absolute-gysin-purity], applied to the zero-dimensional local rings of fields, gives $e_u=0$.

source.place: XVII, proof of Proposition 2.4.3.3, case (1); Stacks Tag 04DF (lemma-universal-homeomorphism) and Tag 04DY (topological invariance)

proof.text: First take a degree-$p$ extension $L=F[z]/(z^p-a)$ in characteristic $p>0$. Its spectrum is the Cartier divisor $D$ in $\mathbf A^1_F$ given by $t^p-a$; compose its Cartier class with the smooth projection orientation, as in Step 3. After applying $Ru_*$, its adjoint is integration of the supported Cartier class. Include $\mathbf A^1_F$ in $\mathbf P^1_F$. The supported-Kummer identity of [lem-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer] identifies the forgotten-support class with $c_1(\mathcal O(D))$. The homogeneous polynomial $T^p-aS^p$ has degree $p$ and no zero at infinity, so its divisor line bundle is $\mathcal O(p)$. Because the Kummer boundary is a group homomorphism, $c_1(\mathcal O(p))=p\,c_1(\mathcal O(1))$. Integration for the orientation of [lem-per-ordinary-smooth-orientation] sends $c_1(\mathcal O(1))$ to $1$, so this adjoint is multiplication by $p$. Under the equivalence in Step 10, adjunction carries that scalar to the same scalar on $\Lambda_L$. This computes the specified class, including its scalar, rather than just an unspecified purity isomorphism.

source.place: XVI, Cartier Kummer normalization and Lemma 2.5.10; XVII, degree normalization in proof of Proposition 2.4.3.3

proof.text: In characteristic $p>0$, take the finite tower $F=F_0\subset F_1\subset\cdots\subset F_n=L$ of degree-$p$ root adjunctions supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-purely-inseparable-pth-root-tower]. Step 11 computes each class as $p$; Step 7 and compatibility of the canonical etale equivalences with composition identify the composite as $p^n$. Field-degree multiplicativity gives $[L:F]=p^n$. This scalar is a unit in $\mathbf F_\ell$ since $p\ne\ell$. For the empty tower, and in characteristic zero where $L=F$, the identity normalization gives $1=[L:F]$.
